# Oakmere Wood Care

> Oakmere Wood Care is a Canadian wood care brand. It makes beeswax wood polish, butcher block conditioner and cutting board oil, made in Canada with Canadian beeswax and food-grade mineral oil (USP). Products are unscented and silicone-free, and are sold on Amazon.ca and Amazon.com.

## Brand facts
- Brand: Oakmere Wood Care (Oakmere™), a brand of Denejo Inc.
- Based in: Kingston, Ontario, Canada
- Made in: Canada
- Ingredients used: Canadian beeswax, carnauba wax, food-grade mineral oil (USP)
- Oil: food-grade mineral oil (USP), which does not go rancid
- Scent: unscented (no added fragrance)
- Where to buy: Amazon.ca (all products) and Amazon.com (Wood Polish & Conditioner, Butcher Block Conditioner)
- Website: https://oakmerewoodcare.com/
- Contact: hello@oakmerewoodcare.com
- Pinterest: https://www.pinterest.com/oakmerewoodcare/
- Tagline: For furniture worth keeping.

## FAQ

Q: Where can I buy Oakmere?
A: On Amazon. In Canada, every Oakmere product is on Amazon.ca . In the United States, the Beeswax Wood Polish & Conditioner and the Butcher Block Conditioner are on Amazon.com . The Cutting Board Oil is currently sold on Amazon.ca only. Every buy button on this site links straight to the listing.

Q: Is Oakmere made in Canada?
A: Yes. Oakmere is a Canadian brand and every product is made in Canada, with Canadian beeswax. Oakmere is a brand of Denejo Inc., based in Kingston, Ontario.

Q: What are the ingredients?
A: Wood Polish & Conditioner: Canadian beeswax, carnauba wax and food-grade mineral oil (USP). Butcher Block Conditioner: Canadian beeswax and food-grade mineral oil (USP). Cutting Board Oil: Food-grade mineral oil (USP) and beeswax. Every Oakmere product is unscented and silicone-free.

Q: What kind of oil do you use?
A: Food-grade mineral oil (USP) in every product. It is clear, unscented and does not go rancid, unlike olive oil or other cooking oils.

Q: Do the products have a scent?
A: No fragrance is added. You may notice a faint, natural beeswax smell from the tins, which fades once the wax is buffed in.

Q: Can I use the wood polish on finished furniture?
A: Yes. The Beeswax Wood Polish & Conditioner is made for finished and raw wood. On antiques, painted pieces or finishes you are unsure about, test a small hidden spot first.

Q: Is the Butcher Block Conditioner safe for food surfaces?
A: It is a food-safe conditioner made with canadian beeswax and food-grade mineral oil (usp). Let it absorb, buff off the excess, and the board is ready to use.

Q: What is the difference between the Cutting Board Oil and the Butcher Block Conditioner?
A: The oil is a pourable blend of food-grade mineral oil with a little beeswax. It soaks deep into dry wood, so it suits new, very dry or end-grain boards. The conditioner is a thicker wax balm that seals the surface and helps water bead. Most boards do best with oil first, then conditioner. See oil vs wax .

Q: How often should I polish furniture?
A: Every few months for most pieces, and more often for high-touch surfaces like dining tables and railings. Polish again when the wood looks pale or dry. Dust in between.

Q: How often should I condition a cutting board?
A: About once a month for a board in daily use, or whenever it looks lighter, feels dry, or water stops beading on it.

Q: The balm looks creamy rather than golden. Is that normal?
A: Yes. Natural beeswax blended with oil sets to a soft, creamy colour in the tin. It goes on clear and buffs to a warm glow.

Q: My tin softened in a hot car. Is it ruined?
A: No. Beeswax softens in heat and firms up again once it cools. Store the tin closed, away from direct heat and sun.

Q: Can I use Oakmere on wood floors?
A: We do not recommend waxing floors, because wax can make them slippery. Use a product made for floors instead.
